{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.", "text": "The wool was cold and heavy, and at first she found nothing but a spent match and a twist of fishing line. Then her fingers closed on paper, folded small and soft as cloth from the lake water. She drew it out carefully, the way she would lift a fledgling from the ground, and carried it to the lamp.

The envelope had come apart along its seams. Inside was a single sheet, and most of the ink had bled into pale blue clouds, but some of the words had held. She could make out *Tuesday* near the top, and lower down, in her father's cramped, leaning hand, *cannot keep it any longer*, and at the very bottom, clear as if it had been written that morning, a name.

Not Harlan's name. Her mother's.

Mary read it twice. Behind her she heard Leonard shift his weight, heard the stove tick as it cooled, heard her own breath going in and out too quickly.

"What does it say?" Leonard asked.

"Nothing," she said. "It's ruined." She folded the sheet along its old creases and held it against her apron, and she did not turn around, because she knew her face would tell him otherwise.

Her mother had been dead nine years. She had gone through the ice in March, a quarter mile out, and they had never found her. Everyone on the lake knew that. Everyone had said so at the burial, standing over an empty box.

On the cot, her father began, very quietly, to weep."}
